post: Keys and values, 8. What training learns

unigram level of TinyStories, bits per b.note: the loss on the held-out stream of n-gram models of orders 1 to 4 counted on the first 200,000,000 training tokens, with interpolated Kneser-Ney smoothing (the dataset's stats.json): upper estimates of the levels H_1 .. H_4; 8.565 bits per token = 5.937 nats, divided by 4.0278 held-out bytes per token. The entropy of the maximum-likelihood unigram table of the whole training set is 8.569 bits per token (2.127 bits per byte).

training tokens at which pico's held-out.note: pico's loss on 1,024 held-out windows at its 21 checkpoints is above the level at 458,752 tokens and below it at 720,896; interpolated in log tokens the crossing is at 605,558 tokens (step 9.2 of 8,240).

minimum over checkpoints of pico's mean.note: KL(n-gram predictor || model) between next-token distributions, at every position of the held-out windows, averaged; the unigram and the bigram predictor are the maximum-likelihood tables of all 542,905,221 training tokens (their own entropies are under `predictors`). The smallest of the 21 checkpoints' means, 0.772 bits = 0.535 nats, is at step 11 (720,896 tokens), where the model's held-out loss is 5.162 nats; at step 0 the divergence is 2.378 nats and at the end 8.759.

bigram level of TinyStories, bits per by.note: the loss on the held-out stream of n-gram models of orders 1 to 4 counted on the first 200,000,000 training tokens, with interpolated Kneser-Ney smoothing (the dataset's stats.json): upper estimates of the levels H_1 .. H_4; 5.164 bits per token = 3.579 nats, divided by 4.0278 held-out bytes per token. The entropy of the maximum-likelihood bigram table of the whole training set is 5.154 bits per token (1.280 bits per byte).

training tokens at which pico's held-out.note: pico's loss on 1,024 held-out windows at its 21 checkpoints is above the level at 1,835,008 tokens and below it at 2,949,120; interpolated in log tokens the crossing is at 2,466,635 tokens (step 37.6 of 8,240).

minimum over checkpoints of pico's mean.note: KL(n-gram predictor || model) between next-token distributions, at every position of the held-out windows, averaged; the unigram and the bigram predictor are the maximum-likelihood tables of all 542,905,221 training tokens (their own entropies are under `predictors`). The smallest of the 21 checkpoints' means, 0.459 bits = 0.318 nats, is at step 28 (1,835,008 tokens), where the model's held-out loss is 3.825 nats; at step 0 the divergence is 4.748 nats and at the end 4.278.

fraction of the 12,769 pairs used for tr.note: 3,830 of the 12,769 pairs, chosen at random (data seed 0); the other 8,939 are the test set.

weight decay of our modular-addition run.note: AdamW on every parameter, rate 0.001, betas [0.9, 0.98], no schedule.

number of epochs of our modular-addition.note: every step takes the whole training set, so a step is an epoch.

epoch at which training accuracy first r.note: the first logged step at which all 3,830 training pairs are right, and they stay right; the logged step before it is 140 (99.9%). measured at 301 log-spaced steps, so each epoch is known to the spacing of the log. (99% of the training pairs are right from step 136: the figure's readout quotes that step.)

test accuracy at that epoch.note: 3.3% of the 8,939 held-out pairs at step 144.

epoch at which test accuracy first excee.note: 99.3% at step 8129; the logged step before it is 7916 (97.5%). 56 times the epoch of 100% training accuracy.

key frequencies of our model's embedding.note: the frequencies holding at least a tenth of the strongest one's power in the trained embedding; by falling power [49, 10, 47, 33, 1]. Together 99.2% of the embedding's power at the end. Nanda et al. report 14, 35, 41, 42, 52 for their seed.

pico's held-out bits per byte.note: the run's final evaluation on its fixed held-out windows (summary.json: 1.5398 nats per token, divided by ln 2 and by 4.0278 held-out bytes per token).

megabytes of information in the TinyStor.note: 542,905,221 tokens x 4.0278 bytes x 0.5515 bits per byte / 8 / 10^6.

training tokens of gpt-pp's main run.note: summary.json of the run: 20,345 steps on 3 cards, one pass.

megabytes of information in gpt-pp's tra.note: 2,999,992,320 tokens x 4.6283 bytes x 0.9429 bits per byte (the run's final held-out evaluation) / 8 / 10^6.

gptpp-base.note: 384 windows of held-out text of 1024 tokens, each inside one document; the loss near position t is the mean over the positions within a quarter of t (a single position over 384 windows is too noisy to subtract). 256 sequences of 50 random tokens written twice after <|bos|>, uniform over the 32,717 tokens that occur in the training set; the second copy is scored without its first token. Bits per token; first and last checkpoint.

pico.note: 1024 windows of held-out text of 256 tokens, each inside one document; the loss near position t is the mean over the positions within a quarter of t (a single position over 1024 windows is too noisy to subtract). 256 sequences of 50 random tokens written twice after <|bos|>, uniform over the 4,009 tokens that occur in the training set; the second copy is scored without its first token. Bits per token; first and last checkpoint.
